critical_findings.finding: Unsafe rendering of Markdown, especially with raw HTML enabled or without blocking schemes like `javascript:`, creates a cross-site scripting (XSS) risk. A user could inadvertently include malicious content from an external source in their notes, which would then be executed in the browsers of anyone viewing the generated site.

Path traversal vulnerabilities during file ingestion could allow the tool to read and publish sensitive files from outside the specified notes directory (e.g., by following symlinks or `../../` paths). This constitutes a critical data leak from the user's local machine into a publicly accessible static site.

Ambiguity in parsing link and tag syntax (e.g., wiki-links vs. relative paths, frontmatter vs. inline tags) can cause incorrect link resolution, missing backlinks, and broken tag navigation. This data integrity failure undermines core features and makes the generated site unreliable for navigating notes.

A non-deterministic build process (due to factors like unstable sorting of files or locale-dependent operations) can produce different outputs on subsequent runs with the same input. This creates noisy, meaningless diffs, breaking git-based deployment workflows and undermining trust in the build process.

The tool may fail at scale. A large number of notes can cause excessive build times and memory usage, or generate a client-side search index so large that it severely degrades the site's initial load time and search responsiveness, rendering the tool ineffective for its intended purpose.

Lack of a rigorous dependency management process, including version pinning and vulnerability scanning, exposes the tool to supply chain risks. An update to a third-party component (e.g., Markdown parser) could silently introduce security vulnerabilities or breaking changes, destabilizing the entire application.

Failure to correctly handle asset and link pathing when hosted in a sub-directory (e.g., `example.com/notes/`). Hardcoded root-relative links (`/style.css`) will break, rendering the site unusable on common static hosting platforms like GitHub Pages, severely limiting its deployability.

In an incremental build/watch mode, a failure to correctly identify all files affected by a change can lead to a partially updated, stale site. For example, editing a note's title may not update links to it on other pages, creating data inconsistencies and a confusing experience for the author.
